newsitem.title: CHINA: LME metals seen range-bound, riding strong copper.
newsitem.headline: LME metals seen range-bound, riding strong copper.

text.p: Base metals looked headed for a quiet week on the London Metal Exchange with most range-bound, though industrial action at a number of copper producers could see some red metal movement, Asia-based traders said on Monday.
Aluminium was seen heading towards $1,650 in the short term, though one trader in Singapore said it needed to do some work first.
LME aluminium closed on Friday at $1,613 a tonne, having ranged between a low of $1,594 and a high of $1,614.
While it appears to have successfully breached $1,600, it was seen being held up by copper's strength.

"Most people are a little confused as to where it (aluminium) goes from here as the $1,625 level offers significant resistance and if it does break through there you'll next see it at the $1,650 level," another trading source said.

"I think there is more overhead selling interest in aluminium than there is in some of the other metals in that it seems to be more fundamentally balanced -- buyers on the dips, sellers on the rally," he said.
Copper finished the Friday p.m. kerb at $2,383 a tonne, up $15, with prices having generally held steady in the face of technical tightness and falling LME stocks.
Brandeis brokers said key resistance was now at $2,440.
Labour disputes at Escondida, Quebrada Branca and Phelps Dodge, as well as the maintenance shutdown of Kennecott's smelter were seen as copper's fundamental props.
Zinc was seen pushing through $1,280, having closed on Friday at $1,275 a tonne.
"In the short term, maybe it will stay range-bound between $1,240 and $1,280," the Singapore source said.
